items.title: Buddy Tate interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995
items.q: Andy Kirk had more of a sweet band, people like Pha Tarrell, and Mary Lou [Williams].

ctx.x: So you say that feel is more relaxed?

More relaxed but still swing. It was more swinging. And they was just having fits and jumping and having fits, and they would be swinging, and those guys would be taking those fine solos and things behind them. And it just swept the whole thing away. It was Chick Webb, well Chick played everything, it had to be up here, you know? It’d be up there, they’d have the midwest swing. Then come Jay McShann after, but they all had a different thing, had a different thing. Andy Kirk had more of a sweet band, people like…

You know I spent some time in that area myself, when you talk about Tulsa, Oklahoma, I spent ten years in Tulsa. And I noticed that the feel is different. It’s more relaxed, it’s got a nice bounce to it, but it doesn’t sound so jumpy and hurried. And it’s still kind of like that.
